units.title: Domain A: Fundamentals of Hospitality Management

outcomes.text: Define hospitality.
Compare the purpose and functions of hotels, restaurants and other hospitality businesses.
Describe the hospitality industry locally and internationally.
Explain hotel facilities such as rooms, restaurants, banquets, spa, conference rooms, business centers, shops and transport.
Map the history and evolution of hotels and lodging.

units.title: Domain B: Career Prospect of the Hospitality Industry

outcomes.text: Classify hospitality career paths in hotels, restaurants, events and tourism.
Analyze the skills and qualifications different hospitality roles need.
Investigate current trends such as technology, changing customer tastes and travel patterns.
Assess how these trends change demand for skills, roles and specializations.

units.title: Domain C: Overview of Departments in Hospitality Industry

outcomes.text: Identify the basic functions of HR in hospitality.
Develop strategies for recruiting, training and keeping hospitality staff.
Evaluate how HR builds a positive culture and handles turnover and talent development.
Identify the basic functions of HR in hospitality.
Develop strategies for recruiting, training and retaining hospitality staff.
Evaluate how HR builds culture, engagement and handles turnover and talent development.
Identify event customers as B2B or B2C.
Tell apart corporate events, conferences, parties, weddings and business meetings.
Describe key parts of the health and safety environment in hospitality.
Explain key parts of food safety for quality and compliance.
Evaluate why internal audits matter for quality.

units.title: Domain E: Sustainable Hospitality

subtopics.title: Tourism links and the T&T Index

outcomes.text: Recognize links between tourism basics, the hospitality index and related dynamics.
Explore the components and indicators of the Tourism and Travel Index.
Analyze how T&T Index rankings relate to hotel performance, visitors, occupancy and economic impact.

units.title: Domain B: Career Prospect of the Hospitality Industry

outcomes.text: Investigate current and emerging hospitality trends.
Assess how trends affect demand for skills and roles.
Predict challenges that hospitality employees face.

units.title: Domain C: Overview of Departments in Hospitality Industry

outcomes.text: Describe basic functions of IT.
Identify how IT improves services and the guest experience.
Explain why cyber security matters in hospitality.
List security principles: risk assessment, threat analysis and best practice.
Analyze security measures such as access control, cameras and alarms that protect guests, staff and property.
Match customers to events as B2B or B2C.
Recognize STP, value propositions and customer journey mapping.
Analyze the role of digital marketing in hospitality.

units.title: Domain D: Department Overview for the Hospitality Industry

outcomes.text: Identify sections and types of kitchen.
Describe culinary basics and cooking techniques.
Identify cuisines served in hotels.
List facilities at a hotel's health club, spa and gym.
Identify types of spa services.
Assess why good communication improves customer service.

units.title: Domain E: Sustainable Hospitality

outcomes.text: Evaluate water management and recycling strategies for sustainable hospitality.
Explain sustainable plantation practices in hospitality.
Predict innovative food and beverage experiences and future trends.
Analyze how innovative food and beverage affects brand, competitiveness and guest satisfaction.
Analyze factors behind technology integration, using data analytics and predictive tools to improve business and decisions.

units.title: Domain A: Fundamentals of Hospitality Management

outcomes.text: Describe the industry's characteristics, scope, segments and role in the global economy.
Analyze how hotels, restaurants and spas relate to each other.
Trace key milestones in the history of hotels and lodging.
Evaluate how social, economic, technological and cultural factors shaped hotels.
Describe hotel facilities: rooms, dining, banquets, spa, business centers and transport.
Categorize hotel departments and their roles in smooth operation.
Understand hotel shifts: morning, general, evening, night and flexi.
Define hospitality and tourism and explain how they depend on each other.
Analyze how tourism growth changes demand for hospitality.
Apply strategic management to combine hospitality and tourism services.
Plan how a hotel can meet tourists' needs with cultural sensitivity and sustainability.
Make a personal career plan with goals, skills and trends.
Evaluate career paths and plan for continued growth and adaptability.
Identify industry challenges such as sustainability, inclusion, crisis management and technology.
Develop ethical solutions to these challenges using best practice.

units.title: Domain B: Human Resource and Organizational Development in the Hospitality Industry

outcomes.text: Explain levels and grades of hospitality staff, from managers to casual workers.
Describe each level's roles and why a clear hierarchy helps.
Analyze strategies for recruiting and hiring hospitality staff.
Weigh recruitment methods like job portals, social media, networking and referrals.
Do pre-hiring tasks: job descriptions, screening and interviews.
Analyze factors in workforce planning for expansion or seasons.
Plan staffing needs, skill gaps and recruiting, training or temporary solutions.
Use forecasting methods suited to hospitality.
Analyze factors behind pay decisions.
Evaluate monetary and non-monetary perks in attracting and keeping staff.
Design a full employee benefits package.
Analyze the role of KPIs and objectives in managing performance.
Design measurable KPIs for different hospitality roles.
Conduct fair, constructive year-end appraisals.
Analyze why diversity and inclusion matter in hospitality.
Evaluate the impact of bias and discrimination.
Discuss ways to build an inclusive culture with equal career access.
Analyze what motivates hospitality employees.
Apply motivational theories to performance and job satisfaction.
Examine causes of employee turnover.
Propose retention strategies for those causes.
Manage notice periods and separations legally and ethically.
Explain why training programs matter for performance and guests.
Design staff development covering hard and soft skills.

units.title: Domain C: Role of Finance in Hospitality Management

outcomes.text: Create and manage budgets using financial data, benchmarks and goals.
Forecast using historical data and market trends to guide decisions and resources.
Interpret financial models and KPIs for planning, risk and performance.
Evaluate financial information to recommend financial plans and decisions.
Explain financial insights clearly to non-financial stakeholders.
Maintain the general ledger so records are accurate and current.
Keep financial records: record transactions, reconcile accounts and follow accounting standards.
Manage accounts payable and receivable, invoices, payment schedules and cash flow.
Reconcile transactions using double-entry accounting and spot discrepancies.
Develop, apply and monitor credit policies to limit risk and raise revenue.
Monitor and control operating costs while keeping quality.
Find and apply cost-saving measures without hurting service.
Follow the purchasing process: purchase requisitions, quotations, purchase orders, receiving and inspecting supplies.
Manage vendors: evaluate suppliers, use cost-effective procurement and run vendor surveys.
Identify salary components such as allowances, overtime, advances, provident fund, EOBI and tax, and how each is calculated.
Understand how payroll adjustments change overall pay.
Analyze revenue streams like rooms, spa, dining, conferences and weddings, with pricing and cross-selling.
Understand how online marketplaces and e-commerce drive bookings, and plan to use online channels.
Control inventory: systems, stock levels, turnover and carrying costs.
Further finance outcome (text cut off in the source after its code).

units.title: Domain D: Role of IT in the Hospitality Industry

outcomes.text: Use software to manage reservations, check-in and check-out, room assignment and billing.
Describe how online booking platforms improve guest service, marketing and emerging technology use.
Explain smart room technology: IoT devices and automated lighting, temperature and entertainment.
Explore how IoT in rooms improves satisfaction and efficiency, and how to match guest preferences.

units.title: Domain E: Kitchen Production in Hospitality

outcomes.text: Describe a kitchen's structure and the roles of the executive chef, sous chef, chef de cuisine, pastry chef and others.
Describe culinary arts basics, cooking techniques and cultural influences.
Create basic recipes: pick ingredients, scale servings and consider cost.
Learn baking and pastry basics: cake decoration, bread, simple confectionery and the science of baking.
Use and sharpen knives and cut safely and efficiently.
Operate and clean culinary equipment safely.
Demonstrate baking, roasting, sauteing and grilling.
Prepare traditional stocks, sauces and soups.
Tell knives and cuts apart and know hot-kitchen methods like braising, frying, poaching and grilling.
Distinguish hot from cold kitchens.
List major cuisines and the diversity of world cooking.
Analyze international cuisines by ingredients, techniques and culture.
Describe food safety and sanitation, handling and storage, with an intro to HACCP.
Explore the science of cooking: ingredient properties and chemical reactions.
Illustrate efficient storage and inventory management.
Illustrate strategic menu engineering for profit and customer preference.

units.title: Domain F: F&B (Food and Beverage) Service in Hospitality

outcomes.text: Present menus in a clear, appealing way.
Set tables attractively with correct utensil, plate and glass arrangement.
Arrange and garnish dishes attractively.
Handle customer complaints with patience, listening and problem solving.
Upsell and cross-sell to enhance the guest experience.
Collect guest feedback and use it to improve service.

units.title: Domain G: Sustainable Hospitality

outcomes.text: Describe sustainable practices: energy efficiency, waste, recycling, water, plantation and lower emissions.
Apply sustainable building and design principles.
List green certifications such as LEED and regional eco-labels, and why they matter.

units.title: Domain A: Role of Engineering in Hospitality

outcomes.text: Carry out routine maintenance and repairs in guest rooms and see why timely upkeep matters.
List inspection methods for building exteriors, including roof, windows and doors.
Maintain facility systems: lighting, power distribution, generators and UPS, HVAC, boilers, water heating and plumbing.

units.title: Domain B: Role of Security in Hospitality

outcomes.text: Describe surveillance and access control systems in hospitality security.
Examine how security patrols deter incidents and build a sense of safety.
Explain CCTV basics: installation, maintenance and monitoring.
Use video analytics to detect threats and review CCTV footage.
Illustrate emergency response plans, common scenarios and staff training.
Describe coordinating with local authorities in emergencies, with drills.
Describe fire risk assessments.
Maintain fire safety equipment with regular checks.
List key features of staff fire evacuation training.
List ways to monitor and secure parking areas.
Describe ways to handle vehicle security issues.

units.title: Domain C: Role of Events in Hospitality

outcomes.text: Categorize events: corporate, social, conferences, weddings and exhibitions.
Plan event setups, including logistics, space design and resources.
Illustrate banquet setups: buffet, plated, family-style and cocktail.
Use event sales techniques: prospecting, proposals and closing deals.
Negotiate by understanding client needs and finding mutually good solutions.

units.title: Domain D: Role of Sales and Marketing in the Hospitality

outcomes.text: Understand marketing strategy with the STP model and the 7Ps.
Distinguish B2B from B2C marketing approaches.
Map the customer journey and craft value propositions.
Apply CRM strategies to personalize and strengthen customer relationships.
Plan and run event marketing and work with the media.
Apply digital marketing: social media, content, SEO and online presence.
Understand how online travel agencies affect bookings, revenue and reach.

units.title: Domain E: Role of Rooms Division in the Hospitality Industry

outcomes.text: Understand room makeup, cleaning standards and in-room amenities such as the minibar.
Meet housekeeping service standards for rooms, public spaces and uniforms.
Take housekeeping orders and run housekeeping audits.
Run guest relations and communication center operations.
Examine guest feedback with complaint handling, surveys and service recovery.
Run front desk services: check-in and check-out, cancellation and no-show policies, and overbooking.
Handle laundry stages: receiving, tagging, washing, ironing and delivery.

units.title: Domain F: Health and Wellness

outcomes.text: Keep gyms and swimming pools safe, clean and enjoyable.

units.title: Domain G: Quality and Compliance

outcomes.text: Use water, waste and energy efficiently and reduce environmental impact.
Apply fire safety: fire types, extinguishers, drills and emergency procedures.
Manage workplace hazards and carry out OHS risk assessments.
Provide first aid and emergency response.
Uphold food safety in handling, storage and preparation.
Keep food and personal hygiene standards.
Run food audits using HACCP and the 4Cs of food safety.
Carry out regular inspections and audits of service quality.
Monitor and improve guest satisfaction using feedback.

units.title: Domain H: Laws and Ethical Considerations

outcomes.text: Understand legal aspects like licensing, labor, privacy, consumer protection, intellectual property, environment and tax.
List and apply labor and employment laws.
Protect guest privacy and data under the law.
Practice integrity, transparency and responsible decision-making with guests, staff and stakeholders.

units.title: Domain I: Future Trends in Hospitality

outcomes.text: Be aware of global trends and cultural differences in hospitality.
Offer unique, culturally immersive guest experiences.
Plan to expand wellness offerings like spa, fitness and mindfulness.
Use wellness-focused design with natural light and elements.
Explain wellness technology, especially for sleep and well-being.
Plan and carry out innovative food and beverage experiences.
Use guest data analytics to personalize experiences.
Explain IoT for smart rooms and operational efficiency.
